items.title: ANTENNE ANTENNE
items.description:
Made together with Lukas Moland, as part of the master graduation show of Oslo National Academy of The Arts, exhibited at Kunstnernes Hus, Oslo. \
Through the understanding of otters is based on a cast of a taxidermied otter standing above the entrance of the gallery.\
Text from exhibition handout: The Scandinavian otter is a shy animal.
And it turns out that it has unwillingly become a container for our forever chemicals. As a result of being at the top of the food chain, it sometimes ends up in the laboratory as a measure of those of our sins that circulates through the ocean and gradually accumulate in its body over time.
We realize that we do not know what this otter is stuffed with. What we have dealt with is the shell of an animal whose body lives an afterlife that exists beyond its soul. Placed on an island of habitat, separating it from the floor on which we stand, it is unclear what landscape it is gazing at. We fill its incomplete presence with concrete. “*Concrete is our destiny — at least as long as it has not been replaced by something else and simpler. (…)*” was written about the exhibition Art in Concrete, which opened at Kunstnernes Hus in 1965. At that time, concrete was introduced into art, and every night, during the 18 days it takes to cast as many otters as there are artists in this exhibition, we sleep surrounded by it. Photo 2,3 by Jacky Jaan-Yuan Kuo. Press mentions: Aftenposten, 24.06.2026 <https://www.aftenposten.no/kultur/i/wrKvVn/antenne-antenne-masterutstilling-paa-kunstnernes-hus-utforsker-fellesskap>

items.title: Everybody should have at least one eye closed
items.workTitle: Everybody should have at least one eye closed
items.medium: Construction wood, metal, pre-owned; tarp, plissé blind, blackout roller blind, venetian blind and A4 print
items.description:
Presented at Pachinko, Oslo.
The exhibition consists of the three sculptures Indent 1, Indent 2 and Indent 3 (danish; *Indfald 1, Indfald 2, Indfald 3*), alongside the letter *Dear Isa*. The work explores the architecture that frames the individual through the structures that surround and cover the window, treating them as a perceptual or mental space within a shared environment. The window blind is approached as a material condition that shapes experience. And while mimicking the temporary window coverings that is seen attached to facades during renovation, the sculptures are detached from architecture and stands as autonomous structures, producing a paradoxical interior of their own.\
The title of the exhibition reconfigures the premise articulated in Isa Genzken’s exhibition Everyone needs at least one window (1992). Where Genzken invokes the window as a condition of possibility Everybody should have at least one eye closed proposes a gesture of skepticism in response to a state of overexposure. Referring back to the body as an important point of view in an increasingly mediated world, the title suggests a need for focus while remaining critical. Like looking through a peephole it narrows attention to something specific, while also recalling the act of looking through a camera lens, seeing the world through images.

items.title: Bliss (blinds)
items.venue: P0 at Oslo National Academy of The Arts
items.medium: Assorted window blinds collected in Oslo through giveaways on finn.no, construction wood, various found objects
items.description:
Presented at P0, Oslo National Academy of The Arts. \
A structure of window blinds forms a corridor diagonally through the exhibition space. Gaps between the lamellas of the blinds allow views to the adjacent space, where the light setup casts shadows that reflect both the scene and the act of looking.

Part of the annual summer exhibition at Arden Asbæk, Copenhagen, revolving around broken love.\
Pocket dream repairing the moment explores the mirror as an intimate space abandoned by the body.

items.title: Efterglød
items.description:
Part of the group exhibition Efterglød - an annual exhibition by Sydhavn Teater and ST:ART, presenting video works in public spaces throughout the neighborhood of Sydhavn, Copenhagen. 
Mount Etna is based on text fragments and footage recorded during a trip to the volcano in Sicily. Overlapping events unfold as tourists descend the slope, creating clouds of dust, and a heat wave drives thousands of ladybugs up the volcano, where they become trapped with nothing to eat. Meanwhile, a forest fire delays airplanes from taking off.

items.title: 19:00 ON TIME
items.medium: Chalk, extracts from personal diary, Iphone notes etc.
items.description:
Text work made as part of the performance event 19:00 ON TIME developed together with Line Rolf, Lukas Moland and Steinar Brovold Hauge at the top floor of the parking garage Bergen Bygarage.\
\
As the event was defined by the boundaries of a parking lot as a public gray zone, the text pieces, written in chalk, would remain only for as long as it took for rain and passing cars to wear them away.

items.workTitle: Without any resistance they spin, they should all just spin, exposing the ground, quick turn in the air with your shoes on
items.medium: Sound piece, nylon strap, bricks, paraffin wax and various parts of motorcycle protective gear
items.title: Melange
items.description:
Part of the bachelor graduation exhibition at Bergen Art Academy. \
The work consists of a sound piece and a sculptural installation presented inside an elevator. The sound piece, recorded by Karen Werner, is based on a manual describing how to change a car's wheel. While the words and sentences have been reconfigured, the text, which initially appears instructional, unfolds into a sensual, almost nonsensical language. The installation consists of a sculptural compilation of parts from motorcycle protective gear, cast together in paraffin wax, and a fixture that holds down the integrated elevator seat. Documentation photos by Ylva Teigen Aas

items.workTitle: *It’s lying there along with the tree, maybe we’ll see him later*
items.venue: Tag Team Studio and Galleri Flig
items.medium: Various concrete types, charcoal on paper, construction wood, construction foil, water and leaves from fountains in Bergen
items.title: *It’s lying there along with the tree, maybe we’ll see him later*
items.description:
Duo project made together with Line Rolf, exhibited in two different parts at Tag Team Studio and Galleri Flig.\
\
The project explores the elements that define the cityscape and how ordinary urban objects gradually become part of its visual and cultural landscape. Based on recordings of shadows found around in the city of Bergen, the works imagines new forms and narratives for city monuments. The works consists of an outdoor sculptural video screening and an installation of concrete casted reliefs of the silhouettes of parked and crashed electric scooters. Documentation photos by Dan Brown. Followed by stills from the video.
